1.why: The UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with clearly generous letter and line spacing across all screenshots.

2.why: No italics or all-caps appear in instructions; text is limited to short, non-dense phrases and labels.

3.why: The single-column layout with large tap targets and uncluttered spacing is readable and well suited to a mobile viewport.

4.why: All instructions are brief plain-language sentences such as “Start your security setup” and “Take as long as you need.”

5.why: The six-digit code field shows the example placeholder 123456 and the login screen shows demo credential examples.

6.why: Every screen contains only short sentences or single-line prompts; no long text blocks must be read to continue.

7.why: No copy-to-clipboard control is present for the identity code (shown only in the browser console) or any other secret.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry appears on any of the five screens.

9.why: Standard email and password inputs are used on the login screen, which browsers and password managers can autofill; the code field is a normal text input.

10.why: A progress bar, bold step heading, and prominent blue primary button make the current step and main action unmistakable.

11.why: Each screen presents exactly one primary action (Sign in, Get identity code, or Check code) with secondary options clearly de-emphasized.

12.why: Green status banners explicitly state what just happened and what to do next after every successful action.

13.why: A “Re-request identity code” button and the ability to re-enter and re-check the code are always available with no penalty indicated.

14.why: The error “That code does not match. Check the six digits, or request a new code.” names the problem and the fix without blame.

15.why: The interface itself states “There is no reading timer. Take as long as you need” and no countdown or expiry is shown.
